heroHeadline: PLA Surges to 22 Sorties on May 7 (18 Cross Median Line, N/C/SW/E ADIZ) — Sharp Re-Escalation From Zero-Sortie Day; 6 PLAN Vessels; 7 Days to Trump-Xi Beijing Summit
heroSubtitle: PLA executed a dramatic reversal on May 7, surging from zero sorties (May 6, first zero-sortie day since pre-May 2 record) to 22 sorties with 18 of 22 crossing the Taiwan Strait median line into northern, central, southwestern, and eastern ADIZ sectors simultaneously — the second-highest non-exercise single-day count on record, behind only May 2's all-time non-exercise record of 29 sorties. 6 PLAN vessels + 1 official ship continued maritime operations around Taiwan. The multi-sector geometry (N+C+SW+E simultaneously) mirrors the May 2 (29 sorties), April 26 (28 sorties), and April 21 (24 sorties) patterns, confirming PLA's deliberate pre-summit escalatory signaling cycle. A Washington Post report on May 7 confirmed China has explicitly signaled Taiwan as the top priority agenda item for the May 14-15 Beijing summit — a departure from Xi's previous approach of setting Taiwan aside in talks with Trump. Beijing is expected to press Trump to limit US arms sales to Taiwan and oppose Taiwanese independence; Taiwan Deputy FM Francois Wu has expressed Taipei is 'most afraid of being put on the menu.' Taiwan's defense budget floor vote is legally eligible from May 8 after the fourth cross-party negotiation round collapsed without consensus on May 6. The $14B PAC-3/NASAMS arms package remains on hold pending the summit outcome.
